compatibility.detail: New attention kind model-drift in client-v0 attention (schema enum and generated clients updated). It is not an alert and offers no actions. It is negotiated on its own: only sessions sending x-st3-features model-drift-attention.v1 (the regenerated Rust and TypeScript clients and the web gateway's defaults) receive it as is. Every other session, including existing clients that send custom-subjects.v1, receives it as an agent-request with no actions. The Swift client does not advertise it yet and reads the mapped form. The population attention metric gains a model-drift kind label. No claim, registry or stored-format change.

manual.detail: A person sees drifting agents they own in fractal alerts ls (under updates) and Now's today group as one item; nothing to do beyond fixing the provider or the declaration.

recovery.detail: Read-derived: rolling back removes the item with no state left behind; the per-seat drift faults are unchanged.

replay.detail: No replay change: the item is derived at read time from the existing per-seat drift failures.

rules.detail: While any agent a person owns has a current harness-model-drift failure (declaration and incarnation fences applied), that person's attention holds exactly one model-drift item. It counts the drifting agents, names the declared and live model when all share one, gives the time since the first drift and the oldest agent, and lists every agent. It changes as agents start or stop drifting and disappears when none drifts. The oldest drifting agent is its source, so its host publishes it. Per-seat drift faults stay agent faults and never become person items.

schema.detail: client-v0 attention_kind enums gain model-drift; no SQL migration.

summary: A person now sees one aggregated inbox item while any agent they own runs on another model than it declares, updated as the set changes and cleared automatically.
